jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

Docker is looking for a Senior Sales Enablement Program Manager to design and produce the training and enablement content that powers our Go-To-Market (GTM) team. Reporting to the Head of Sales Enablement, you will work cross-functionally with Product Marketing (PMM), Product, Marketing, technical subject matter experts — including our AI Governance (AIG) overlay team — and GTM leaders to identify content needs, build clear requirements, and produce field-ready content — documents, videos, Mindtickle courses, quizzes, and certifications — that fuels GTM execution, effectiveness, and accuracy.

This role takes real technical understanding: you’ll need to get comfortable with how Docker’s product works — including newer, more technical areas like AI Governance — and translate that technical depth into simple, sales-ready value positioning the field can use with confidence. This isn’t a fully technical role, but it does require the curiosity and aptitude to learn technical features well enough to explain them simply.

This is a hands-on, creative role for someone who loves translating complex technical ideas into clear, engaging learning experiences, and who cares just as much about keeping content easy to find as they do about making it great. If you enjoy partnering across teams, building a single source of truth for enablement content, and making sure the field can always find what they need, this role is for you.

Responsibilities

Content Needs & Requirements

  • Partner with PMM, Product, Marketing, technical subject matter experts, and GTM leaders to identify content needs and translate them into clear requirements.

  • Turn input from Sales and cross-functional stakeholders into structured content briefs and production plans.

  • Prioritize content requests based on business impact, GTM execution needs, and field urgency.

Content Production

  • Write, design, and produce enablement content across formats: documents, playbooks, one-pagers, and decks.

  • Build and maintain courses, quizzes, and certifications for onboarding and ongoing training within Mindtickle.

  • Develop scripts, storyboards, and recordings for training and demo videos in partnership with subject matter experts.

  • Partner with our AI Governance (AIG) overlay team to produce enablement content — feature walkthroughs, FAQs, talk tracks, and battle cards — that translates technical AI Governance capabilities into clear, sales-ready value positioning.

  • Build content that reinforces and extends Docker’s Command of the Message sales methodology, ensuring messaging, positioning, and value language stay consistent across all enablement materials.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with PMM, Product, Marketing, and technical subject matter experts to ensure content is accurate, timely, and aligned to launches and positioning.

  • Partner with GTM leaders to make sure training collateral supports GTM execution, effectiveness, and accuracy in the field.

  • Build a working technical understanding of Docker’s product — including AI Governance and other technical capabilities — directly from teams like AIG, then translate that understanding into content the field can use with confidence.

  • Serve as a liaison between Sales and Product, Marketing, and PMM to keep content grounded in what the field actually needs.

Content Governance & Findability

  • Own a single source of truth for enablement content, retiring duplicates and outdated material as new content ships.

  • Organize and tag content so it’s easy to search and find within Mindtickle and other systems, for both Sales and the broader GTM audience.

  • Maintain a consistent voice, structure, and visual standard across all enablement content.

  • Use completion data, quiz results, and field feedback to identify what’s working and what needs to be reworked.

Qualifications

Required

  • 4+ years of experience creating content in a sales enablement, marketing, instructional design, or training role, ideally in SaaS.

  • Strong technical aptitude and curiosity — comfortable building a working understanding of Docker’s product and features (including more technical areas like AI Governance) and translating that understanding into simple, sales-ready value positioning. This role does not require deep engineering expertise, but does require the ability to learn technical concepts and explain them simply.

  • Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to turn complex or technical information into clear, engaging content.

  • Experience producing video content, from scripting through basic editing.

  • Comfort building courses, assessments, or certifications in an LMS (Mindtickle experience a plus).

  • Proven ability to manage multiple content projects at once and hit deadlines without sacrificing quality.

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills — you can work with PMM, Product, Marketing, technical subject matter experts, and GTM leaders, and manage competing priorities.

  • Experience organizing content so it’s easy to search, find, and trust as a single source of truth.

  • Excellent attention to detail and a strong sense of visual and brand consistency overall.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience creating enablement content for technical, platform, or security/governance-related features (e.g., access controls, compliance, or AI governance).

  • Hands-on experience with Mindtickle or a similar sales enablement/LMS platform.

  • Experience with video recording/editing tools (e.g., Camtasia, Vidyard, Loom).

  • Familiarity with SaaS sales motions and Command of the Message or similar frameworks.

  • Experience organizing content libraries or knowledge bases — tagging, taxonomy, and search — in a CMS or LMS.

  • Background in graphic design or presentation design.

  • Exposure to containerization, DevOps tooling, or developer platforms (Docker experience a significant plus).

What to Expect

We believe in setting people up to win. Here’s what great looks like in this role:

First 30 Days — Learn & Listen

  • Ramp on Docker’s products, GTM motion, and existing enablement content library.

  • Meet with PMM, Product, Marketing, and GTM leaders to understand current content gaps.

  • Get up to speed on Mindtickle and the team’s other content and enablement tools.

First 90 Days — Take Ownership

  • Own production of at least one major piece of enablement content, start to finish, in partnership with PMM, Product, or Marketing.

  • Ship enablement content for at least one technical feature or launch — potentially in partnership with the AIG overlay team — translating it into clear value positioning.

  • Begin organizing the content library so it’s easier to search and find.

First Year — Drive Impact

  • Be the go-to owner for enablement content production, trusted by PMM, Product, Marketing, and GTM leaders.

  • Maintain a single source of truth for content that’s current, easy to navigate, and consistently used by Sales and the broader GTM audience.

  • Use engagement and feedback data to continuously raise the bar on content quality and findability.

Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

 

Compensation & Equity

Canada: CA$184,450– CA$263,500 + equity

United States: $133,000 – $190,00 + equity

  • Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

  • AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

  • Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

If you enjoy partnering across teams, building a single source of truth for enablement content, and making sure the field can always find what they need, this role is for you.




RESPONSIBILITIES

Content Needs & Requirements

 - Partner with PMM, Product, Marketing, technical subject matter experts, and GTM leaders to identify content needs and translate them into clear requirements.

 - Turn input from Sales and cross-functional stakeholders into structured content briefs and production plans.

 - Prioritize content requests based on business impact, GTM execution needs, and field urgency.

Content Production

 - Write, design, and produce enablement content across formats: documents, playbooks, one-pagers, and decks.

 - Build and maintain courses, quizzes, and certifications for onboarding and ongoing training within Mindtickle.

 - Develop scripts, storyboards, and recordings for training and demo videos in partnership with subject matter experts.

 - Partner with our AI Governance (AIG) overlay team to produce enablement content — feature walkthroughs, FAQs, talk tracks, and battle cards — that translates technical AI Governance capabilities into clear, sales-ready value positioning.

 - Build content that reinforces and extends Docker’s Command of the Message sales methodology, ensuring messaging, positioning, and value language stay consistent across all enablement materials.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

 - Work closely with PMM, Product, Marketing, and technical subject matter experts to ensure content is accurate, timely, and aligned to launches and positioning.

 - Partner with GTM leaders to make sure training collateral supports GTM execution, effectiveness, and accuracy in the field.

 - Build a working technical understanding of Docker’s product — including AI Governance and other technical capabilities — directly from teams like AIG, then translate that understanding into content the field can use with confidence.

 - Serve as a liaison between Sales and Product, Marketing, and PMM to keep content grounded in what the field actually needs.

Content Governance & Findability

 - Own a single source of truth for enablement content, retiring duplicates and outdated material as new content ships.

 - Organize and tag content so it’s easy to search and find within Mindtickle and other systems, for both Sales and the broader GTM audience.

 - Maintain a consistent voice, structure, and visual standard across all enablement content.

 - Use completion data, quiz results, and field feedback to identify what’s working and what needs to be reworked.




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - 4+ years of experience creating content in a sales enablement, marketing, instructional design, or training role, ideally in SaaS.

 - Strong technical aptitude and curiosity — comfortable building a working understanding of Docker’s product and features (including more technical areas like AI Governance) and translating that understanding into simple, sales-ready value positioning. This role does not require deep engineering expertise, but does require the ability to learn technical concepts and explain them simply.

 - Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to turn complex or technical information into clear, engaging content.

 - Experience producing video content, from scripting through basic editing.

 - Comfort building courses, assessments, or certifications in an LMS (Mindtickle experience a plus).

 - Proven ability to manage multiple content projects at once and hit deadlines without sacrificing quality.

 - Strong cross-functional collaboration skills — you can work with PMM, Product, Marketing, technical subject matter experts, and GTM leaders, and manage competing priorities.

 - Experience organizing content so it’s easy to search, find, and trust as a single source of truth.

 - Excellent attention to detail and a strong sense of visual and brand consistency overall.

Strongly Preferred

 - Experience creating enablement content for technical, platform, or security/governance-related features (e.g., access controls, compliance, or AI governance).

 - Hands-on experience with Mindtickle or a similar sales enablement/LMS platform.

 - Experience with video recording/editing tools (e.g., Camtasia, Vidyard, Loom).

 - Familiarity with SaaS sales motions and Command of the Message or similar frameworks.

 - Experience organizing content libraries or knowledge bases — tagging, taxonomy, and search — in a CMS or LMS.

 - Background in graphic design or presentation design.

 - Exposure to containerization, DevOps tooling, or developer platforms (Docker experience a significant plus).




WHAT TO EXPECT

We believe in setting people up to win. Here’s what great looks like in this role:

First 30 Days — Learn & Listen

 - Ramp on Docker’s products, GTM motion, and existing enablement content library.

 - Meet with PMM, Product, Marketing, and GTM leaders to understand current content gaps.

 - Get up to speed on Mindtickle and the team’s other content and enablement tools.

First 90 Days — Take Ownership

 - Own production of at least one major piece of enablement content, start to finish, in partnership with PMM, Product, or Marketing.

 - Ship enablement content for at least one technical feature or launch — potentially in partnership with the AIG overlay team — translating it into clear value positioning.

 - Begin organizing the content library so it’s easier to search and find.

First Year — Drive Impact

 - Be the go-to owner for enablement content production, trusted by PMM, Product, Marketing, and GTM leaders.

 - Maintain a single source of truth for content that’s current, easy to navigate, and consistently used by Sales and the broader GTM audience.

 - Use engagement and feedback data to continuously raise the bar on content quality and findability.



Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

United States: $133,000 – $190,00 + equity

jobs.title: Staff Sales Engineer, Strategic Accounts (EMEA)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

We're looking for a Staff Sales Engineer who's energized by solving hard, emerging problems at the intersection of AI, security, and software delivery. You will act as a trusted technical advisor and champion owner, partnering closely with Account Executives, Post Sales, and Product teams to drive measurable business and technical value through:

  • Technical Selling and Deal Shaping

  • AI Governance and Security Thought leadership

  • Technical Champion Ownership and Thought Leadership

  • Customer and Internal Advocacy

  • Competitive and Strategic Selling

This role suits people who like translating deep technical complexity into business clarity, who are comfortable being one of the first to help define a category, and who bring varied backgrounds and ways of thinking to how we solve customer problems.

As a Staff Sales Engineer, you will be reporting to the Solutions Engineering leadership team and operate at the intersection of technical depth, business acumen, and competitive selling discipline.


Responsibilities

Technical Selling and Deal Shaping

Lead deep technical discovery across Platform Engineering, DevOps, Security, and AI/ML teams to understand:

  • AI governance requirements for agentic development (shadow AI, ungoverned MCP tools, agents holding real developer credentials)

  • Software supply chain risk posture

  • Regulatory and compliance drivers (e.g., EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework)

  • Secure development lifecycle requirements

Shape technical requirements early in the sales cycle to align customer outcomes with Docker's differentiated value in AI governance, container security, and software supply chain integrity.

Design, position, and execute structured PoCs/PoVs focused on:

  • Sandbox, network, and MCP tool policy enforcement

  • Image and artifact integrity (Docker Hardened Images, SLSA Build Level 3 provenance, verifiable SBOMs)

  • Software supply chain visibility

  • Agent and MCP tool governance controls

  • Secure build pipelines

Define clear success criteria, evaluation frameworks, and executive-ready value summaries.

Influence decision-making through demos, workshops, architecture reviews, and technical executive briefings.

Translate complex AI security and governance capabilities into clear business value narratives for CISOs, Heads of Platform Engineering, and AI leaders.

AI Governance and Security Thought Leadership

Establish credibility as a trusted advisor on:

  • Responsible AI development practices

  • Secure AI model lifecycle management

  • Software supply chain integrity (SLSA provenance, SBOMs, verified base images)

  • Container and artifact security

  • DevSecOps best practices

Guide customers in implementing governance controls across AI-enabled SDLC workflows.

Provide architectural guidance for:

  • Agentic AI development environments and runtime isolation (sandboxing)

  • Policy-as-code enforcement across agents, tools, and machines

  • MCP tool governance and allow-listing

  • Identity and access governance for AI workloads (IdP-based role and policy assignment)

  • Audit, logging, and SIEM visibility for agent activity

Act as a subject matter expert on secure software supply chain and AI security trends in customer-facing engagements.

Technical Champion Ownership and Thought Leadership

  • Build, own, and expand relationships with technical champions across Security, DevOps, Platform, and AI teams.

  • Establish credibility as a trusted advisor through technical thought leadership, architectural guidance, and industry best practices.

  • Leverage champion relationships to influence broader buying groups, shape requirements, and uncover cross-sell and expansion opportunities.

  • Maintain engagement beyond the initial sale, ensuring outcomes are realized and leveraging insights to support future sales motions.

Customer and Internal Advocacy

  • Advocate for customer needs with Product and Engineering, providing clear, actionable feedback informed by field experience.

  • Coordinate with Post Sales and Support resources to ensure continuity across the customer lifecycle.

  • Develop reusable technical assets (workshops, demos, reference architectures, enablement content) to scale impact across accounts.

Competitive and Strategic Selling

  • Actively support competitive sales motions by identifying differentiation and influencing evaluation criteria throughout the sales cycle.

  • Partner with Sales to develop technical win strategies for strategic and competitive accounts.

Qualifications

We know strong candidates come from a range of paths, and that confidence gaps keep some excellent candidates from applying to roles like this. If you meet most of what's below and are excited about the rest, please apply.

  • Experience as a Sales Engineer, Solutions Engineer, or Solutions Architect in complex enterprise sales.

  • Strong experience running competitive PoCs/PoVs with clearly defined success and exit criteria.

  • Ability to engage credibly with senior technical and business stakeholders, including security and platform leadership.

  • Solid understanding of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), containers, DevOps, and modern application architectures.

  • Experience with Docker, container ecosystems, or adjacent technologies strongly preferred.

  • Development, agentic AI development, software development lifecycle, and/or software supply chain experience strongly preferred.

  • Familiarity with AI governance, secure software supply chain (SLSA, SBOMs), MCP or agentic tooling, and DevSecOps practices strongly preferred.

  • Must be fluent in English.

  • Excellent communication, influence, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Willingness to travel to customer sites up to 25%.

What to Expect

First 30 days

  • You will be welcomed with a first-in-class onboarding experience that includes equipment setup, a sweet swag package, and a collaborative training program working with an onboarding peer.

  • You will learn how to navigate award-winning sales tools such as Salesforce, Opine, Sigma, and Docker.

  • You will actively engage with senior stakeholders and manage relationships with clients.

  • You will work closely with your peers and partner with SEs to develop strategies to advocate for our customers.

  • At the end of your first month, you will have a proficient grasp of the tools and activities necessary to be successful in your role.

First 60 days

  • You will be laser-focused on supporting the sales teams during your second month.

  • You will have connected with all of your team members.

  • You will gain in-depth knowledge of Docker's products and how they impact our customers.

  • You will have an advanced understanding of tools, activities, and best practices to be successful in your role.

First 90 days

  • In month three, you will be confident in your craft and ready to immerse yourself fully in our customers' business needs.

  • You will continue efforts to improve messaging, processes, and activities.

  • You will educate our clients about our product roadmap and undertake product training for users.

  • You will be ready to operate independently at full speed.

Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

 

Compensation & Equity

EU: €141,400– €202,000 OTE + equity

______________________________________________________________________

Posting Information

  • Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

  • AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

  • Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________

Perks & Benefits

  • Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

  • Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

  • Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

  • Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

  • Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

  • Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

  • Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

  • Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

  • Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

  • Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.

Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community.

jobs.title: Principal Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

Docker Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) embed directly with our most strategic customers to solve important, complex technical problems and turn ambitious ideas into production outcomes. FDEs take on the most challenging technical challenges using existing Docker products and patterns when possible, and work across customer, Docker Product and Engineering teams to realize new approaches when required.

 

As a Docker FDE, you will work side-by-side with customer engineering teams to deeply understand their goals, problems, constraints, and technical landscape; identify the highest-leverage opportunities; and design, build, and ship solutions with them. You own the technical journey from discovery and architecture through prototyping, implementation and production rollout.

 

The solutions you build may use existing Docker products, extend Docker into new environments, integrate deeply with customer and third-party systems, or reveal capabilities that Docker should build next. You work closely with Docker Solutions Architects to evolve existing patterns, and Docker Product and Engineering to turn new learnings into reusable patterns and product capabilities.

 

Responsibilities

Build in Production with Customers

  • Embed with customer engineering teams to design, build, and ship solutions from first prototype through stable production rollout. Use existing Docker products and patterns when possible, invent, prototype and validate innovative solutions when necessary.

  • Deliver working technical artifacts to customers: custom MCP servers with tightly integrated Docker Sandbox environments for coding agents and containerized agents; Docker Compose definitions for multi-agent harnesses and model-backed applications; Hardened Image standardization and migration; New tools that unblock customer progress.

  • Integrate Docker's AI platform with the customer's existing stack, including identity providers (OIDC/SAML/SSO), secrets management, private and air-gapped registries, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and observability tooling.

  • Own technical delivery on your engagements: scope the work, sequence it, make trade-offs between speed and quality, remove blockers early, and contribute directly to code whenever progress depends on it.

Make AI Adoption Safe and Governable

  • Translate customer security, compliance, and platform requirements into concrete plans and see those plans through from ideation to production.

  • Help customers define controls to enable them to adopt agentic AI to solve their unique business problems without compromising security, compliance, data sovereignty or end-user experience.

  • Establish quality and performance standards for customers and work closely with Docker Product and Engineering to quickly address issues that fall outside of established thresholds

  • Partner with customer security and platform teams to get agentic workloads through architecture review, threat modeling, and change control.

Partner with Solutions Architecture and the Field

  • Work closely with Solutions Architects to enable off-the-self solutions when possible and provide technical experience and leadership when a bespoke solution is necessary.

  • Feed implementation learnings back into reference architectures, SOW templates, and success patterns so that FDE innovations become standard features and implementation patterns.

  • Support the field with technical depth during proofs of concept, escalations, and expansion conversations when a working build is the fastest path to a customer adoption.

Close the Loop with Product and Engineering

  • As part of Docker Engineering FDEs work closely with Product and Engineering teams to fold FDE innovations, learnings, and design patterns into existing or new products and services.

  • Work with Customers, Product and Engineering to establish quality and performance thresholds, ensuring customer environments meet them consistently, and responding quickly and decisively when they don’t.

  • Be the voice of the customer. Deliver data-driven and actionable feedback to Product and Engineering: what works well; what does not; what customers are asking for; and what blocks their adoption and forward progress. FDE experience directly influences the roadmap.

Shape the Practice

  • Define the FDE engagement model, delivery standards, and quality bar, and codify them so that engagements are consistent across customers, regions, and delivery partners.

  • Mentor and lead other Forward Deployed Engineers, and participate in hiring loops to grow the team.

  • Act as the senior technical escalation point on the hardest problems impacting your customers. Every incident is an opportunity to improve Docker products and services.

  • Maintain deep, current knowledge of the agentic AI stack: LLMs, APIs, MCP, coding agents, model and harness evaluation approaches, performance and quality thresholds, deployment patterns.

  • This role may require participation in an on-call rotation to provide support outside of standard business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as needed.

 

Qualifications

Required

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Professional Services Engineer, or Software Engineer with consulting or technical founder experience.

  • Technical leadership across multiple engagements, teams, or domains, with a proven ability to set delivery standards, define repeatable patterns, and influence product direction through field evidence.

  • Expert production coding skills in Go, Python, or TypeScript, with a track record of shipping and operating software that other people depend on and of leading technical design reviews.

  • Deep, hands-on Docker expertise: Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, Docker Compose, image and registry operations, container networking and storage, and container security fundamentals.

  • Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agents in production, including tool use and function calling, the Model Context Protocol (MCP server and client implementation), prompt and context engineering, and evaluation of agent behavior.

  • Working knowledge of software supply chain security: SBOMs, image signing and attestation, vulnerability management, minimal and hardened base images, and secure CI/CD.

  • Experience integrating with enterprise systems: identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, LDAP/Active Directory), federated identity protocols (OIDC, SAML), secrets managers, Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP).

  • Ability to scope and deliver complex work in ambiguous, fast-moving customer environments, making sound trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality.

  • Excellent communication skills with engineers, security and platform teams, and executive stakeholders, with a low-ego, collaborative approach and the ability to lead through influence rather than authority.

  • Proven track record of technical mentorship and of raising the bar for the engineers around you.

  • High agency and comfort operating autonomously in distributed, remote-first teams.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Travel to customer sites to build in person with customer teams, estimated at up to 50%.

Bonus

  • Experience with Docker Hardened Images, Docker Scout, MCP Gateway, MCP Toolkit, Docker Sandboxes, or Docker Model Runner.

  • Experience deploying and operating coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or similar) in team or enterprise settings.

  • Experience with air-gapped, regulated, or compliance-driven environments in financial services, healthcare, government, or similar sectors.

  • Contributions to open source projects in the container, Kubernetes, or MCP ecosystems.

  • Prior experience founding or scaling a Forward Deployed Engineering or Professional Services practice.

Docker considers visa sponsorship on a case-by-case basis based on business needs.

 

Compensation & Equity

United States: $198K – $319K + equity

  • AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

______________________________________________________________________

Perks & Benefits

  • Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

  • Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

  • Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

  • Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

  • Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

  • Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

  • Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________



Docker Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) embed directly with our most strategic customers to solve important, complex technical problems and turn ambitious ideas into production outcomes. FDEs take on the most challenging technical challenges using existing Docker products and patterns when possible, and work across customer, Docker Product and Engineering teams to realize new approaches when required.

 

As a Docker FDE, you will work side-by-side with customer engineering teams to deeply understand their goals, problems, constraints, and technical landscape; identify the highest-leverage opportunities; and design, build, and ship solutions with them. You own the technical journey from discovery and architecture through prototyping, implementation and production rollout.

 

The solutions you build may use existing Docker products, extend Docker into new environments, integrate deeply with customer and third-party systems, or reveal capabilities that Docker should build next. You work closely with Docker Solutions Architects to evolve existing patterns, and Docker Product and Engineering to turn new learnings into reusable patterns and product capabilities.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

Build in Production with Customers

 - Embed with customer engineering teams to design, build, and ship solutions from first prototype through stable production rollout. Use existing Docker products and patterns when possible, invent, prototype and validate innovative solutions when necessary.

 - Deliver working technical artifacts to customers: custom MCP servers with tightly integrated Docker Sandbox environments for coding agents and containerized agents; Docker Compose definitions for multi-agent harnesses and model-backed applications; Hardened Image standardization and migration; New tools that unblock customer progress.

 - Integrate Docker's AI platform with the customer's existing stack, including identity providers (OIDC/SAML/SSO), secrets management, private and air-gapped registries, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and observability tooling.

 - Own technical delivery on your engagements: scope the work, sequence it, make trade-offs between speed and quality, remove blockers early, and contribute directly to code whenever progress depends on it.

Make AI Adoption Safe and Governable

 - Translate customer security, compliance, and platform requirements into concrete plans and see those plans through from ideation to production.

 - Help customers define controls to enable them to adopt agentic AI to solve their unique business problems without compromising security, compliance, data sovereignty or end-user experience.

 - Establish quality and performance standards for customers and work closely with Docker Product and Engineering to quickly address issues that fall outside of established thresholds

 - Partner with customer security and platform teams to get agentic workloads through architecture review, threat modeling, and change control.

Partner with Solutions Architecture and the Field

 - Work closely with Solutions Architects to enable off-the-self solutions when possible and provide technical experience and leadership when a bespoke solution is necessary.

 - Feed implementation learnings back into reference architectures, SOW templates, and success patterns so that FDE innovations become standard features and implementation patterns.

 - Support the field with technical depth during proofs of concept, escalations, and expansion conversations when a working build is the fastest path to a customer adoption.

Close the Loop with Product and Engineering

 - As part of Docker Engineering FDEs work closely with Product and Engineering teams to fold FDE innovations, learnings, and design patterns into existing or new products and services.

 - Work with Customers, Product and Engineering to establish quality and performance thresholds, ensuring customer environments meet them consistently, and responding quickly and decisively when they don’t.

 - Be the voice of the customer. Deliver data-driven and actionable feedback to Product and Engineering: what works well; what does not; what customers are asking for; and what blocks their adoption and forward progress. FDE experience directly influences the roadmap.

Shape the Practice

 - Define the FDE engagement model, delivery standards, and quality bar, and codify them so that engagements are consistent across customers, regions, and delivery partners.

 - Mentor and lead other Forward Deployed Engineers, and participate in hiring loops to grow the team.

 - Act as the senior technical escalation point on the hardest problems impacting your customers. Every incident is an opportunity to improve Docker products and services.

 - Maintain deep, current knowledge of the agentic AI stack: LLMs, APIs, MCP, coding agents, model and harness evaluation approaches, performance and quality thresholds, deployment patterns.

 - This role may require participation in an on-call rotation to provide support outside of standard business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as needed.

 


QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - 10+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Professional Services Engineer, or Software Engineer with consulting or technical founder experience.

 - Technical leadership across multiple engagements, teams, or domains, with a proven ability to set delivery standards, define repeatable patterns, and influence product direction through field evidence.

 - Expert production coding skills in Go, Python, or TypeScript, with a track record of shipping and operating software that other people depend on and of leading technical design reviews.

 - Deep, hands-on Docker expertise: Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, Docker Compose, image and registry operations, container networking and storage, and container security fundamentals.

 - Hands-on experience building with LLMs and agents in production, including tool use and function calling, the Model Context Protocol (MCP server and client implementation), prompt and context engineering, and evaluation of agent behavior.

 - Working knowledge of software supply chain security: SBOMs, image signing and attestation, vulnerability management, minimal and hardened base images, and secure CI/CD.

 - Experience integrating with enterprise systems: identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, LDAP/Active Directory), federated identity protocols (OIDC, SAML), secrets managers, Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP).

 - Ability to scope and deliver complex work in ambiguous, fast-moving customer environments, making sound trade-offs between scope, speed, and quality.

 - Excellent communication skills with engineers, security and platform teams, and executive stakeholders, with a low-ego, collaborative approach and the ability to lead through influence rather than authority.

 - Proven track record of technical mentorship and of raising the bar for the engineers around you.

 - High agency and comfort operating autonomously in distributed, remote-first teams.

 - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Travel to customer sites to build in person with customer teams, estimated at up to 50%.

Bonus 

 - Experience with Docker Hardened Images, Docker Scout, MCP Gateway, MCP Toolkit, Docker Sandboxes, or Docker Model Runner.

 - Experience deploying and operating coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or similar) in team or enterprise settings.

 - Contributions to open source projects in the container, Kubernetes, or MCP ecosystems.

 - Prior experience founding or scaling a Forward Deployed Engineering or Professional Services practice.

  • You will have connected with all of your primary customer accounts (both net-new opportunities in flight and partner with Renewal Managers on upcoming renewals)

  • Build prospecting lists for target accounts, understanding key decision-makers and then reach out to them using all communication channels (cold call, email, chat, and social media)

  • You will comprehend and maintain in-depth knowledge of Docker’s products and have a great pitch

  • Adhere to team KPI metrics and prospecting standards

  • You will have an advanced understanding of tools, activities, and best practices to be successful in the AE role

  • You will ideally be able to close your first transaction

  • You will continue efforts to improve messaging, processes, and daily activities

  • You will be an accomplished seller of Docker products with multiple transactions (renewals, upsell, net-new) under your belt

  • You will be ready to independently operate at full speed

  • Develop a high-level regional reseller strategy and engagement plan

  • Launch initial joint sales and marketing initiatives with reseller partners

  • Drive partner enablement and define clear co-sell and deal engagement workflows

  • Build durable, high-value relationships with strategic and regional reseller partners

jobs.title: Senior Lifecycle Marketing Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

Docker's Product-Led Growth (PLG) team owns turning product usage into revenue across the full Platform: the Container business (Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, Docker Build Cloud, Docker Scout) and the AI business (Sandboxes, AI Governance, Model Runner, MCP Toolkit, MCP Catalog). Lifecycle marketing is one of the fastest-scaling parts of that team: it already owns user and admin nurtures, renewal automation, and first-touch outreach for PQLs and inbound leads, running against a marketable base in the tens of millions.

As Senior Lifecycle Marketer, you'll report directly to the VP of PLG and partner closely with our existing lifecycle marketing lead. You'll take ownership of assigned products, audiences, and lifecycle stages, with real input into shaping the approach for what you own, not just shipping someone else's plan, and you'll help turn a fast-growing list of priorities into a structured, scalable lifecycle engine.

What Makes Someone Successful in This Role

  • Lifecycle Fluency: You think in full user journeys, not campaigns. You've done lifecycle marketing specifically, not just growth or demand gen, and you know how nurture, activation, retention, and renewal connect across a product's full lifecycle.

  • Builder's Mindset: You'd rather own a program end to end, strategy, build, QA, and send, than hand pieces of it off. You bring structure to ambiguity: turning a fast-growing list of priorities into themes, a build queue, and a sequenced roadmap.

  • Audience & Signal Validation: You know how to validate an audience and its underlying signal before it ships: spot-checking record-level data, sanity-checking targeting logic, and catching a bad segment before it reaches users. You don't need to write SQL yourself, but you can work directly with data teams to confirm a list is right.

  • Cross-Functional Operator: You operate well across marketing, sales (BDR and renewals), data, and design/agency partners, and you know how to keep programs moving even when you don't own every dependency.

  • Marketing Automation Execution: You've personally built campaigns in Marketo or an equivalent platform, not just briefed them: audience builds, suppressions and contact governance, pre-send QA and live proofs, and launch monitoring, including troubleshooting a broken data sync in the moment.

  • Technical Translation: You can take a technical product or a raw usage signal, a feature adoption event, a usage threshold, a new capability, and turn it into messaging that reads credible to a developer or admin, not generic marketing copy.

Responsibilities

  • Build the Lifecycle Engine: Own and build lifecycle campaigns (email and in-product messaging) across Docker's Container and AI Platform products, including Sandboxes and AI Governance, for both end users and admins.

  • Scale Programmatic Sends: Design and run large-scale programmatic sends, such as recurring account health checks, to a base in the tens of millions, working within the team's marketing automation stack (currently Marketo and Mailgun; expect a platform transition in the next 6–12 months).

  • Automate Lead and Renewal Motions: Stand up and run automated first-touch flows for PQLs and inbound leads, in partnership with BDR and renewals stakeholders.

  • Validate Audiences & Signals: Partner with data and growth engineering to pull the usage signals campaigns depend on (Snowflake and internal data tools), and validate that an audience and its underlying signal are correct before every send.

  • Manage Suppressions & Contact Governance: Own suppression lists and contact governance rules so campaigns stay compliant and don't over-message or reach the wrong audience.

  • QA, Launch Monitoring & Troubleshooting: Run pre-send QA and live proofs on every campaign, monitor launches as they go out, and troubleshoot issues in real time, including broken data syncs.

  • Translate Signals into Messaging: Turn technical product usage and adoption signals into messaging that reads credible and useful to developers and admins, not generic marketing copy.

  • Shape and Sequence Strategy: Take a fast-growing list of priorities and turn it into a concrete build queue: itemize the work, sequence it, and flag capacity or dependency issues early.

  • Coordinate Design & Agency Partners: Work with design and agency partners to keep campaign quality and turnaround on track.

  • Operationalize Reporting: Own naming, tracking, and reporting on programs so the rest of the team has visibility into what's live, what's next, and what it's driving.

Qualifications

  • Lifecycle Marketing Experience: A background specifically in lifecycle marketing, not pure growth or demand gen, ideally inside a PLG or self-serve motion.

  • Proven Program Ownership: A track record of owning campaigns end to end (strategy, build, QA, send) and shipping programs that moved a real metric: activation, retention, or renewal conversion.

  • Marketing Automation Build Experience: Hands-on build experience in Marketo or an equivalent marketing automation platform: audience builds, program/campaign setup, suppressions and contact governance, pre-send QA and live proofs, and launch monitoring.

  • Data & Targeting Validation: Comfortable working directly with data teams to validate record-level data and targeting logic, for example auditing who's actually in a segment or spot-checking a list against expectations. Writing SQL yourself is a plus, not a requirement.

  • Technical-to-Message Translation: A track record of turning a technical product or a raw usage signal into messaging that reads credible to a developer or admin audience, not generic marketing copy.

  • Technical Familiarity: Comfort navigating developer ecosystems, cloud infrastructure, or complex multi-product software platforms.

  • Independent Ownership: Senior-level judgment and ownership as an individual contributor: you can run with ambiguity and drive a program without every step spelled out, and you collaborate well with another senior peer on the team.

What to Expect

First 30 Days

  • Immerse & Align: Get up to speed on Docker's PLG motion, product surface area (Container and AI), and the programs lifecycle already owns. Build a working relationship with data, BDR, renewals, and design/agency partners.

  • Program & Tooling Audit: Audit the current state of user and admin nurtures, renewal automation, and PQL/lead outreach, and get familiar with the Marketo/Mailgun stack and its upcoming transition.

  • Roadmap Calibration: Work with the lifecycle team to turn the current priority list into themes, a build queue, and a sequenced roadmap.

First 90 Days

  • Ship Owned Campaigns: Take ownership of at least one full program, such as an admin nurture flow or a PQL first-touch sequence, from build through send.

  • Contribute to Renewal Automation: Stand up a first version of automated renewal outreach in partnership with the renewals team.

  • Build the Reporting Cadence: Put in place naming, tracking, and reporting so the team has clear visibility into what's live and what it's driving.

One Year Outlook

  • Own a Mature Program Set: Own a mature, scaled set of lifecycle programs across your assigned products, audiences, and lifecycle stages.

  • Prove Impact: Show measurable lift in activation, retention, or renewal conversion tied directly to your programs.

  • Scale the Function: Help lifecycle marketing operate as a predictable, automated engine rather than a set of one-off campaigns, as scope keeps expanding across the Platform.

Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

 

Compensation & Equity

Canada: CA$160,300– CA$229,000 + equity

United States: $115,500 – $165,000 + equity

______________________________________________________________________

Posting Information

  • Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

  • AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

  • Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________

Perks & Benefits

  • Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

  • Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

  • Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

  • Home office support – Set up your workspace for comfort and success.

  • Technology stipend – Equivalent to US$100 net per month to help support your work.

  • Learning & development – Annual stipend for conferences, courses, certifications, and continued learning.

  • Parental leave – 16 weeks of paid parental leave after six months of employment.

  • Equity for all full-time employees – Share in Docker's long-term success as we continue to grow.

  • Comprehensive benefits – Medical, retirement, and paid holidays vary by country.

  • Docker swag – Because representing the whale never gets old.

Docker is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects a broad range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe diverse teams build better products, make better decisions, and better serve our global community.

 - Translate Signals into Messaging: Turn technical product usage and adoption signals into messaging that reads credible and useful to developers and admins, not generic marketing copy.

 - Shape and Sequence Strategy: Take a fast-growing list of priorities and turn it into a concrete build queue: itemize the work, sequence it, and flag capacity or dependency issues early.

 - Coordinate Design & Agency Partners: Work with design and agency partners to keep campaign quality and turnaround on track.

 - Operationalize Reporting: Own naming, tracking, and reporting on programs so the rest of the team has visibility into what's live, what's next, and what it's driving.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Lifecycle Marketing Experience: A background specifically in lifecycle marketing, not pure growth or demand gen, ideally inside a PLG or self-serve motion.

 - Proven Program Ownership: A track record of owning campaigns end to end (strategy, build, QA, send) and shipping programs that moved a real metric: activation, retention, or renewal conversion.

 - Marketing Automation Build Experience: Hands-on build experience in Marketo or an equivalent marketing automation platform: audience builds, program/campaign setup, suppressions and contact governance, pre-send QA and live proofs, and launch monitoring.

 - Data & Targeting Validation: Comfortable working directly with data teams to validate record-level data and targeting logic, for example auditing who's actually in a segment or spot-checking a list against expectations. Writing SQL yourself is a plus, not a requirement.

 - Technical-to-Message Translation: A track record of turning a technical product or a raw usage signal into messaging that reads credible to a developer or admin audience, not generic marketing copy.

 - Technical Familiarity: Comfort navigating developer ecosystems, cloud infrastructure, or complex multi-product software platforms.

WHAT TO EXPECT

 - Roadmap Calibration: Work with the lifecycle team to turn the current priority list into themes, a build queue, and a sequenced roadmap.


FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Ship Owned Campaigns: Take ownership of at least one full program, such as an admin nurture flow or a PQL first-touch sequence, from build through send.

 - Contribute to Renewal Automation: Stand up a first version of automated renewal outreach in partnership with the renewals team.

 - Build the Reporting Cadence: Put in place naming, tracking, and reporting so the team has clear visibility into what's live and what it's driving.


ONE YEAR OUTLOOK

 - Own a Mature Program Set: Own a mature, scaled set of lifecycle programs across your assigned products, audiences, and lifecycle stages.

 - Prove Impact: Show measurable lift in activation, retention, or renewal conversion tied directly to your programs.

 - Scale the Function: Help lifecycle marketing operate as a predictable, automated engine rather than a set of one-off campaigns, as scope keeps expanding across the Platform.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

The Senior Principal Software Engineer is responsible for shaping and evolving the company’s technical landscape. In addition to designing, developing, and maintaining core systems, the Senior Principal Software Engineer provides strategic guidance to align technology initiatives with business goals. This role is vital in ensuring that the platform is secure, scalable, and performant—capable of supporting rapid growth and driving innovation.

Responsibilities

Technical Strategy & Architecture

● Define and drive the overarching technical vision, ensuring the platform meets current and future scalability, performance, and security needs

● Evaluate and select tools, frameworks, and architectures to maintain a state-of-the-art technology stack

Leadership & Mentorship

● Provide technical leadership and guidance to the engineering organization, setting best practices and standards.

● Coach and mentor engineers, fostering a culture of continuous learning and collaboration

Innovation & Research

● Investigate emerging technologies, frameworks, and best practices

● Lead prototyping initiatives and proof-of-concepts that can transform the platform’s capabilities

Scalability & Performance

● Ensure the platform is designed for high performance and can seamlessly handle increasing user loads

● Oversee performance optimization, load balancing, and capacity planning strategies

Reliability & Availability

● Design fault-tolerant, highly available systems that minimize downtime and deliver a seamless user experience Infrastructure Automation

● Advocate for and implement Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles, CI/CD pipelines, and automation best practices

● Continuously refine deployment, testing, and operations processes to improve efficiency

Security & Compliance

● Collaborate with security experts to ensure platform integrity, compliance with industry standards, and protection of sensitive data

● Proactively address security vulnerabilities and champion secure coding practices

Cross-Functional Collaboration

● Work closely with product managers, designers, and other stakeholders to ensure technical initiatives support business objectives

● Drive alignment between engineering roadmaps and product strategies

Technical Problem-Solving

● Tackle complex architectural and technical issues, providing clear direction and innovative solutions

● Serve as an escalation point for critical system challenges

Code Quality & Reviews

● Uphold coding standards through thorough code reviews, ensuring high-quality, maintainable codebases

● Establish and enforce best practices around testing, documentation, and version control

Documentation & Knowledge Sharing

● Produce comprehensive technical documentation, including architectural diagrams, design guidelines, and operational runbooks

● Promote a transparent engineering culture by sharing insights and successes across the organization

Qualifications

● 12+ years of software engineering experience with demonstrated expertise across multiple domains (SDLC, AI engineering, corporate systems, etc)

● Extensive software engineering experience, with a track record in designing and implementing large-scale, distributed systems

● Deep technical expertise: Proficiency in multiple programming languages, cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), and modern development frameworks

● Leadership acumen: Demonstrated ability to lead diverse engineering teams, inspire innovation, and drive successful outcomes

● Architectural vision: Proven skill in defining and driving architectural roadmaps that align with evolving business needs.

● Problem-solving ability: Expertise in diagnosing complex system issues and designing robust, scalable solutions

● Communication skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of influencing both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

● Security conscious: Solid understanding of security best practices, compliance standards, and data protection

● Continuous improvement mindset: Passion for optimizing processes, toolchains, and workflows

● Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

As a Senior Principal Software Engineer, you will not only architect innovative solutions but also shape the technical culture. Your leadership and expertise will be pivotal in building a resilient, cutting-edge platform that supports rapid growth and drives long-term success.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Billing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

We're building AI-native development practices into how this team works at a foundational level. That means infrastructure design needs to account for a new kind of collaborator: AI agents that generate, deploy, and operate software. The Staff Infrastructure Engineer on this team will keep systems running, define what safe, observable, AI-assisted infrastructure operations look like in practice, and set the standard for how the broader engineering organization follows.

What you'll work on

The Billing Platform Engineering team owns the systems that make Docker's commercial model real. You'll work on problems like:

  • How do we design infrastructure that makes AI-generated deployments safe to ship and easy to roll back?

  • How do we instrument billing systems so that failures — billing miscalculations, entitlement gaps, payment errors — are detected immediately and unambiguously?

  • How do we build infrastructure that scales with usage-based billing workloads without manual intervention?

  • How do we make the developer experience on this team faster and more reliable — local environments, CI/CD pipelines, deployment tooling?

Responsibilities

  • Own and evolve the infrastructure supporting Billing Platform services: compute, storage, networking, CI/CD, and observability

  • Design and maintain IaC (Terraform) for billing system infrastructure on AWS; set module patterns and standards for the team

  • Build and own observability systems — metrics, logging, alerting — with a focus on billing accuracy and payment reliability

  • Define deployment patterns and runbooks that work well in an AI-agent-assisted development workflow: clear rollback procedures, safe promotion gates, automated validation

  • Partner with software engineers on service design — bringing infrastructure constraints and operational requirements into the conversation before code is written

  • Identify systemic risks and drive improvements that span team or organizational boundaries

  • Lead incident response for billing system issues. This role may require participation in an on-call rotation to provide support outside of standard business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as needed.

  • Mentor engineers across the team; your technical judgment should raise the floor for everyone

Qualifications

  • 8+ years in platform, infrastructure, or SRE roles supporting production SaaS systems at scale

  • Deep AWS expertise: ECS or EKS, RDS (Postgres preferred), networking, IAM, cost management — you've operated these systems under real load and real incidents

  • Expert-level Terraform; you've designed reusable module patterns and set standards others follow

  • Experience building and owning observability stacks (Datadog, Grafana, or similar) at an organizational level — not just using them

  • Strong familiarity with CI/CD systems — Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or equivalent — including pipeline design and developer experience ownership

  • Kubernetes at an operational and architectural level

  • A track record of identifying systemic risks and driving improvements that span team or organizational boundaries

  • Security-first mindset: threat modeling, blast radius analysis, least-privilege by default, audit trails as a design requirement

  • Strong written English; at Staff level, written communication is how you scale your influence across teams

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

What sets you apart

You don't wait for problems to be handed to you — you find them, frame them, and drive the solution. You've operated at a scope where your decisions affected multiple teams or systems, and you know how to build consensus and move work forward without direct authority. You've thought seriously about what infrastructure needs to look like when AI agents are generating and shipping code — safe deployment patterns, strong observability, clean rollback — and you want to help define that standard here. Experience with billing, payments, or financial systems infrastructure is a meaningful plus.

What to Expect
First 30 Days

You will ship code in your first week. We run an agent-first development workflow — infrastructure changes start with a plan, specifications are written before generation, and every change is reviewed before it merges — and onboarding is no exception. You will get hands-on with the infrastructure supporting Billing Platform services early, shadow on-call, and build a clear picture of the system before you start making bigger changes. By the end of 30 days you will have shipped real work and know where the most important problems are.

First 90 Days

You will have taken ownership of one or more infrastructure components and delivered an improvement from design to production with measurable impact. You will be an active participant in deployment and reliability discussions, bringing infrastructure constraints and operational requirements into the conversation early — before code is written. You will be a full participant in the on-call rotation and have begun shaping the team's technical direction.

One Year Outlook

You will be the team's trusted authority on billing infrastructure. You will have driven meaningful improvements to observability, deployment safety, or platform reliability — and your work will be directly visible in the resilience and correctness of systems that handle real financial transactions for millions of Docker users. You will have helped define what AI-agent-assisted infrastructure operations look like done right, and that standard will be visible beyond this team.

Docker considers sponsorship on a case-by-case basis based on business needs.

 

Compensation & Equity

United States: $170,350 – $275,550 + equity

  • Open vacancy: This posting is for an existing open role.

  • AI in hiring: Docker may use AI-assisted tools during our recruiting process.

  • Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________

  • Remote-first by design – Work from your home, with offices in Seattle and Paris for connection and collaboration.

  • Flexibility that fits your life – We trust you to manage your schedule while delivering great work.

  • Time to recharge – Generous PTO, designated quarterly Whaleness Days, and a designated end-of-year Whaleness break.

You've thought seriously about what infrastructure needs to look like when AI agents are generating and shipping code — safe deployment patterns, strong observability, clean rollback — and you want to help define that standard here. Experience with billing, payments, or financial systems infrastructure is a meaningful plus.




WHAT TO EXPECT
FIRST 30 DAYS

You will ship code in your first week. We run an agent-first development workflow — infrastructure changes start with a plan, specifications are written before generation, and every change is reviewed before it merges — and onboarding is no exception. You will get hands-on with the infrastructure supporting Billing Platform services early, shadow on-call, and build a clear picture of the system before you start making bigger changes. By the end of 30 days you will have shipped real work and know where the most important problems are.




FIRST 90 DAYS

You will have taken ownership of one or more infrastructure components and delivered an improvement from design to production with measurable impact. You will be an active participant in deployment and reliability discussions, bringing infrastructure constraints and operational requirements into the conversation early — before code is written. You will be a full participant in the on-call rotation and have begun shaping the team's technical direction.




ONE YEAR OUTLOOK

You will be the team's trusted authority on billing infrastructure. You will have driven meaningful improvements to observability, deployment safety, or platform reliability — and your work will be directly visible in the resilience and correctness of systems that handle real financial transactions for millions of Docker users. You will have helped define what AI-agent-assisted infrastructure operations look like done right, and that standard will be visible beyond this team.

About Docker

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________

The Products Team at Docker is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead components of Docker Sandboxes. You will own and drive this strategic product area from high-level concept design through delivery, adoption, and operation. You will help shape how developers and AI agents use fast, secure, isolated environments across local and cloud workflows. You will work closely with developers inside and outside of Docker, our customers, and our partners to expand our open ecosystem offering and provide value. As the company and ecosystem grow, you will help foster teams eager to continuously build, measure, and learn.

To thrive in this role, you will need experience working with developers, deep technical fluency in systems and developer infrastructure, and prior experience as a software engineer. You will need to understand containers, sandboxes/microVMs, virtualization technologies, hypervisors, the software development lifecycle, and how untrusted or agent-generated code can be safely executed and orchestrated. You will need a relentless drive to try new things and an eye for detail. Your long-term success will depend on your ability to own the product roadmap, earn the trust of the developer community, and scale reliable services. Most importantly, you will need to be comfortable taking ownership of big objectives with big goals, working with a cross-functional team, and maintaining a bias for action.

Responsibilities

  • You own Docker Sandboxes, its long-term vision, roadmap, revenue, adoption, and results.

  • You believe in and can succinctly articulate our customers, their workflows, and their pain points. You empathize with the world they live in and the security, performance, compatibility, and cost constraints they work through.

  • You will engage deeply with developers building AI agents, coding environments, CI and testing systems, and other workloads that require secure, isolated execution, finding solutions for today while optimizing for tomorrow's vision.

  • You enjoy building infrastructure products that are easy to adopt and use. You will turn complex tradeoffs across isolation, startup time, performance, density, networking, storage, and cost into simple product experiences.

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and will guide product definition, feature prioritization, and scope in concert with engineering, design, security, operations, and go-to-market teams.

  • You are a fan of iterative development, working with customers and cross-functional teams to hypothesize, measure adoption and impact, learn from releases, and continually improve the roadmap.

Qualifications

  • You have deep empathy for the needs of developers and are obsessed with talking to your users.

  • You have prior professional experience as a software engineer, ideally in systems, infrastructure, platform engineering, developer tools, or cloud.

  • You have strong technical familiarity with sandboxes/microVMs, containers, virtualization technologies, and hypervisors, including the isolation and security boundaries each provides.

  • You understand the building blocks of modern developer infrastructure, including Linux, container runtimes, orchestration, networking, storage, APIs, and cloud services.

  • You have experience designing, building, or operating systems that execute customer-provided, untrusted, or agent-generated code at scale.

  • You are comfortable interacting with a command-line interface and discussing APIs, SDKs, and technical architecture with engineers and developers.

  • You have experience building B2B or SaaS products, or a background in public cloud and developer infrastructure.

  • You understand software supply chain and software security concerns, including multi-tenant isolation, identity, secrets management, observability, and reliability.

  • You can break down complex technical problems into small, releasable, user-valuable features.

  • You can explain complex ideas simply and communicate effectively in writing, verbally, and visually across diverse stakeholders.

  • You can analyze qualitative and quantitative data to inform decisions, define success metrics, and prioritize investments.

  • You have a collaborative approach, experience running products from greenfield to scale, and the ability to work with fast-moving, distributed, cross-functional teams. You are a doer as well as a strategist; we are small and need all hands on deck.

What to expect
First 30 days

  • Get to know Docker: our vision, mission, and values.

  • Understand the Docker Sandboxes team's mission, product strategy, and technical architecture.

  • Meet the team along with peers across the business unit and company.

  • Work closely with designers, researchers, engineers, security partners, and customers to understand user needs and current pain points.

  • Work with your manager and team to review and create quarterly goals.

  • Understand the product roadmap, key technical and business tradeoffs, and the data available to make data-driven decisions.

First 90 days

  • Understand the company's and business unit's product vision and how Docker Sandboxes contributes to it.

  • Provide clarity on product vision, target users, priority use cases, and how the team contributes to the overall success of Docker.

  • Develop a deep understanding of our developers and customers, how they use isolated environments, and why they choose Docker.

  • Shape the team roadmap and product strategy in close collaboration with design, engineering, security, and go-to-market peers.

  • Lead the definition of team OKRs and success metrics for the quarter, and provide clear progress reports.

One Year Outlook

  • Lead product initiatives across cross-functional teams that make secure, isolated execution simple and valuable for developers and AI agents.

  • Drive the long-term direction of Docker Sandboxes, including improvements to adoption, ecosystem integration, reliability, scale, unit economics, and ARR.

Docker does not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Canada CA$255,500 - CA$365,000 + equity

United States: $184,100 - $263,000 + equity

  • Interview recordings: Candidates will be invited to opt in to interview recordings to support interviewer calibration and consistent evaluations. Recordings are optional and require explicit consent.

______________________________________________________________________
